snippet.title: GOOGLE FULLTIME INTERVIEW PROCESS 2020
snippet.description:
because no coding channel is complete without one

new year new u. go get google fam.

 INSTAGRAM 
https://www.instagram.com/coderbea/ 

 Comics 
https://www.instagram.com/bogwarts/

(Your experience may vary)

Resume Portion
- Cold application! Oftentimes does not work
- No cover letter. Not very common to have one (on a personal note I’ve pretty much never sent one to any major company)

Coding Challenge Portion
- 1.5 hours long with 2 questions
- 1 easier, 2 harder
- Both leetcode mediums
- Can go between the two anytime (different from Amazon)
- Robert allocated 30 minutes for the first and 1 hour for the last one


Onsite Interview portion
- Flew to Mountain View
- Consisted about 5 rounds of coding. 1 hour each.
- ALL CODING. No system design (this was a new grad interview)
- Leetcode medium - Leetcode hards
- Strings, graphs, threads. All different kinds of questions. Problems he saw on here, he never saw on Leetcode
- Lunch interview, showed him around the office,
- Robert did not feel like he passed every single interview but he still got an offer!
- Most companies won’t fail you for not passing one interview

Anything different about google than other places in terms of interviewing?
- they looked into the way he solved problems and cared about his thought process and asked a lot of questions about how he went about a problem. Some companies don’t prod as much. They see a solution, and that’s fine. Google wants to make sure you understand it and how you arrive 
- They gave a pretty general question, and he had to ask the right questions to make it more specific and make the problem space smaller and more manageable
- Google focuses on algorithms (less about data structures)

snippet.title: Palantir Interview Process
snippet.description:
Main Points:

1. Some people say it was the hardest interview ever, I would say it was a Leetcode Medium - Medium-Hard
2. I didn't pass it! But my advice for any open-ended / system design question is to talk about the simplest case first, and make sure you can fully justify that, then expand on it.
3. Make sure you communicate with your interviewer throughout the process!
